decision.explanation: The central register (D-B0LRS, issued 2028-01-11, so current under R3) names Zemun Belnarlo (DOB 1952-08-15) as sole 100% beneficial owner, last updated 2026-06-12. The Business Register shareholder excerpt (D-9N8FK, issued 2028-01-11, Aurelia Business Register) is a tier 1 document that names Rospor Dormirnar (DOB 1992-10-06) as sole 100% shareholder since 2026-10-24, which is after the register's last update. The customer's self-declaration (D-6PHD5, tier 3) matches the business register, not the central register. So the beneficial owners in reliable evidence differ from the register, a discrepancy exists. The default would be to report it, but the request-correction exception does not apply: the customer is rated higher-risk (D-JHDQI), which excludes the exception, and the business register is issued by the same Aurelia authority as the central register, so it is not independent for exception (b). In addition, the internal risk record carries an analyst alert that the ownership chain may have been concealed (D-JHDQI). Under R2 an alert indicating possible concealment requires escalation, and any suspicious-activity decision is reserved for human officers. I am therefore escalating rather than reporting or requesting a correction, and I make no determination on the relationship or on suspicious-activity filing.

The notary and court confirmation mentioned in D-ISLN2 is not in the file and was not relied on.

The central register entry (D-X3QYJ, issued 2027-12-25, so current under R3) names Rosda Daroslo as the sole beneficial owner (100%). The only other evidence is the customer's self-declaration (D-MO6V4, tier 3), which names Venwen Mirlowen (100%) and asserts that a notary and court confirmed an ownership change. That assertion is not backed by any tier 1 or 2 document in the file: the notarial deed and court record are not available. Under R2, the register cannot be verified against itself, and a discrepancy cannot be confirmed or ruled out without a tier 1 or 2 source stating who the beneficial owners are. The determination therefore cannot be made. Reporting to the register or requesting a correction would be premature, since the register may be right or wrong. The correct step is to request the notarial deed and/or court record evidencing the ownership change, which the customer has said exist. The internal record (D-HFDEO) shows a standard rating and no alerts, so there is no concealment indicator requiring escalation at this stage. Once the notarial or court document is received, the determination can be re-run.
